# Results — Study 950 (Zero-Coupon Convexity) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). **Arm A** is 100% of a
zero-coupon Treasury fund (**EDV**, 20-30y STRIPS; **ZROZ** as the cross-check). **Arm B**
is the duration-matched coupon mix, `L` units of **TLT** plus `(1 - L)` units of **BIL**,
with `L` solved from the realised beta of each leg's daily excess return to the **same rate
factor** — the daily change in the 30-year constant-maturity yield (`^TYX`) — over a
rolling 252-day window, read at the last session of month *m* and traded for all of month
*m+1* (**one execution lag**, the only one in the study). Both arms are measured
**excess-of-cash** (minus BIL's total return), so the cash leg cancels in the spread. Daily
**total-return** closes (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`); `^TYX` is a yield level in
percentage points, not a price. Costs: **3 bps one-way x NAV** on the mix's monthly
rebalance turnover. Financing: **25 bp/yr over bills** on the levered part `(L - 1)` of the
mix — a **PROXY/ASSUMPTION**, not a tape input, swept below. Both frictions fall on Arm B
only (Arm A is buy-and-hold), so the race is deliberately tilted **towards** the claim under
test. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| EDV, TLT, BIL, ^TYX | 2009-02-02 → 2026-06-30 | 4,377 days / 208 months | Fingerprint `a669055b6e7a` |

The start is EDV's 2008 inception plus the 252-day beta warmup. ZROZ (from 2010-12) is the
cross-check. Hedge ratio on TLT: mean **L = 1.420**, sd 0.097, range [1.19, 1.62] — the
STRIPS fund runs about **42% more duration** than the coupon long bond, exactly as the
zero-versus-coupon structure implies.

## The duration match works — and that is the first result

| Arm | Mean (excess-of-cash) | Vol | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **A — 100% EDV** | +2.65%/yr | 21.41% | +0.124 | +0.57 |
| **B — duration-matched TLT+BIL** | +3.19%/yr | 21.42% | +0.149 | +0.71 |
| **A − B (the spread)** | **−0.53%/yr** | 4.77% | −0.112 daily / **−0.213** monthly | **−0.87** |

The vol ratio A/B is **1.000**: matching on the realised beta to the 30-year yield really
does equalise the rate risk of the two arms. On the plain average the zero fund **loses**
to the duration-matched coupon mix by 4.0 bp/month (HAC *t* = −1.08, hit rate 44.2%), with
a block-bootstrap 95% CI of **[−11.0, +3.4] bp/month** — indistinguishable from zero, and
certainly not the free lunch a convexity pickup would be.

## The headline — the asymmetry (convexity) regression

`diff_m = a + b1 * dy_m + b2 * Q_m`, monthly, HAC(6) standard errors. `Q` is either the
**squared net monthly move** `dy²` (the textbook second-order term) or the **realised
variance** `sum(dy_t²)` of the daily factor inside the month (the gamma P&L a daily-marked
fund actually accrues). `dy` in decimals.

| Quadratic term | *a* (bp/mo) | *t* | *b1* (residual duration) | *t* | *b2* | *t* | worth at 25 bp / 50 bp | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `dy²` (net move) | **−8.75** | −1.50 | −0.72 (≈ **+0.72 yr**) | **−2.73** | **+110.5** | **+0.84** | +6.9 / +27.6 bp | 0.079 |
| `sum(dy_t²)` (realised var) | **−12.74** | −1.88 | −0.71 (≈ +0.71 yr) | **−2.55** | **+154.7** | **+1.31** | +9.7 / +38.7 bp | 0.084 |

Three things to read off this table.

1. **The signs are what the theory predicts almost everywhere — but not everywhere.**
   `b2 > 0` (the zero leg gains in large-move months) and `a < 0` (it pays for that in quiet
   ones). Across the **full 12-cut census** (two funds × three eras × two quadratic
   specifications — every cut the design implies, printed by `verify.py`, none omitted) that
   holds in **11 of 12** cuts. The twelfth, **ZROZ 2018-2026 on realised variance**, flips
   *both* signs (`b2` = −123.5, `a` = +5.09). See the census table below.
2. **The headline does not clear the bar, and the two cuts that do, do not replicate.**
   The headline is **+0.84** (**+1.31** on realised variance). The largest |*t*| **anywhere
   in the grid** is **+2.88** — ZROZ, realised variance, 2010-2017 — with its `dy²` twin on
   the same 84 months at **+2.14**. Those are the only 2 of 12 cuts to clear 2, they are the
   same 84 months of the *cross-check* fund counted twice, no multiple-comparison correction
   has been applied to twelve uncorrected looks, and the adjacent era of that very fund
   reverses the sign. The headline fund, EDV, never exceeds **+1.87** in any cut. The
   block-bootstrap CI for `b2` is **[−163, +338]** on `dy²` (27.5% of resamples negative) and
   **[−41, +516]** on realised variance (5.9% negative). The desk's bar is a **robust**
   |*t*| ≥ 2 on the real tape; an isolated sub-era of the secondary fund that inverts next
   door is the textbook definition of *not* robust — it is what `WEAK` ("fragile to method
   or selection") is for.
3. **The match leaks.** `b1` is significantly negative (*t* = −2.73), i.e. the "duration-
   matched" spread still carries about **+0.72 years** of residual duration at the monthly
   horizon, and does so in **both** eras (*t* = −2.06 early, −2.41 late). EDV sits at the
   25-30y point of the curve and TLT at ~20y: what looks like a convexity spread is also,
   irreducibly, a **20s-versus-30s curve trade**.

**Breakeven.** Taking the fitted numbers at face value, the convexity term has to repay the
intercept: the spread only turns positive above a **28.1 bp** monthly move in the 30-year
yield (28.7 bp on the realised-variance fit). The **median** month over this sample moved
**15.0 bp**. Convexity is under water in roughly two months out of three even on its own
fitted terms.

## The full cut census — every cut the design implies

An earlier draft of this page reported six cuts and claimed the sign pattern was unanimous
and that "the best *t* anywhere is +1.69". Running the **remaining six** cuts the same
design implies — the two eras of the ZROZ cross-check, which had not been fit — showed both
claims to be wrong: the pattern is 11-of-12, not 12-of-12, and the largest |*t*| in the grid
is **+2.88**, not +1.69. The whole grid is printed by `verify.py` so no future draft can
quote a subset of it. **Nothing below is omitted.**

| Fund | Era | Spec | n | *a* (bp/mo) | *t* | *b2* | *t* | *b1* *t* | |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| EDV | full | `dy²` | 208 | −8.75 | −1.50 | +110.5 | +0.84 | −2.73 | *headline* |
| EDV | full | `rv` | 208 | −12.74 | −1.88 | +154.7 | +1.31 | −2.55 | |
| EDV | early | `dy²` | 106 | −12.78 | −1.44 | +179.9 | +0.85 | −2.06 | |
| EDV | early | `rv` | 106 | −28.44 | −2.19 | +381.5 | +1.87 | −1.98 | |
| EDV | late | `dy²` | 101 | −4.18 | −0.94 | +21.8 | +0.39 | −2.41 | |
| EDV | late | `rv` | 101 | −5.39 | −1.48 | +40.0 | +1.19 | −2.30 | |
| ZROZ | full | `dy²` | 186 | −11.43 | −1.75 | +208.7 | +1.69 | −1.40 | |
| ZROZ | full | `rv` | 186 | −4.72 | −0.46 | +51.7 | +0.27 | −1.39 | |
| ZROZ | early | `dy²` | 84 | −17.13 | −1.90 | **+403.8** | **+2.14** | −0.07 | ← clears 2 |
| ZROZ | early | `rv` | 84 | −33.19 | −2.34 | **+618.9** | **+2.88** | −0.68 | ← clears 2 |
| ZROZ | late | `dy²` | 101 | −6.04 | −0.82 | +78.0 | +0.95 | −1.27 | |
| ZROZ | late | `rv` | 101 | **+5.09** | +0.74 | **−123.5** | −1.81 | −1.26 | ← **both signs flip** |

**Census:** `b2` > 0 in **11/12**, `a` < 0 in **11/12**, |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/12**, largest |*t*|
anywhere **+2.88** (ZROZ, early, `rv`).

How to read it honestly. The two cuts that clear 2 are not two pieces of evidence: they are
one 84-month window of the *cross-check* fund, fit twice with two closely-related
regressors. Twelve uncorrected looks at a null would be expected to throw up roughly one
|*t*| ≥ 2 by chance; we have one *window* that does. And it does not survive its own
neighbour — the same fund in **2018-2026** produces `b2` = −123.5 with a **positive**
intercept, i.e. the exact inverse of the convexity story, on the era that actually contains
2020 and 2022. Meanwhile the primary fund, EDV, is quiet in every cut. That is a signal
"fragile to method or selection", not a signal the tape certifies.

## The rawest form of the claim — move-size buckets

Terciles of the absolute monthly yield move. If convexity were being paid, the right-hand
column should climb from left to right. Both the tercile boundaries and the linear-leak
adjustment in the last column are fitted on the **whole sample** — this table is a
**descriptive** picture of the payoff shape, never a tradable rule, and no return here is
claimed as one.

| Bucket | n | mean \|Δy\| | spread | HAC *t* | hit rate | spread after removing the linear leak |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| quiet | 70 | 4.1 bp | −0.94 bp/mo | −0.15 | 45.7% | −1.22 bp/mo |
| middling | 69 | 14.5 bp | −7.51 bp/mo | −1.22 | 43.5% | −7.07 bp/mo |
| **large** | 69 | **32.4 bp** | **−3.52 bp/mo** | −0.43 | 43.5% | **−2.38 bp/mo** |

It does not climb. The large-move bucket is **negative**, and stays negative after the
residual linear rate exposure is regressed out (an in-sample, descriptive adjustment).
This is not a contradiction of the fitted `b2`. At `b2 = +110.5` the fit predicts the quiet
bucket should earn **+0.27 bp/month** and the large bucket **+12.93 bp/month** — a gap of
**12.7 bp** against a standard error on that gap of **11.6 bp**, i.e. about *one* standard
error. The regression and the bucket table are telling the same story without contradiction:
**the convexity pickup, if it is there at all, sits right at the edge of what 208 months can
resolve.**

## Robustness

**Two eras (split 2018-01-01).**

| Era | n | spread | *t* | *a* (bp/mo) | *t* | *b2* | *t* | *b1* *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-2017 | 106 mo | −4.21 | −0.67 | −12.78 | −1.44 | +179.9 | +0.85 | −2.06 |
| 2018-2026 | 101 mo | −4.17 | −1.18 | −4.18 | −0.94 | **+21.8** | +0.39 | −2.41 |

The spread is equally (in)significant in both halves; `b2` keeps its sign but collapses by
a factor of eight into the recent era — the era that contains 2020 and 2022, the two
largest rate shocks of the sample. The one thing that *is* era-stable is the residual
duration leak.

**Cost sweep** (one-way bps on the mix's turnover — the zero arm pays nothing):

| cost | spread | *t* | *b2* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | −4.00 bp/mo | −1.08 | +110.5 |
| 3 bps | −3.98 bp/mo | −1.08 | +110.5 |
| 25 bps | −3.78 bp/mo | −1.02 | +110.5 |

Turnover is a rounding error: `L` moves a few points a month, so friction never decides
anything here.

**Financing-spread sweep** (the study's only non-tape input; a wider spread makes the
levered mix worse and therefore **flatters** the zero leg):

| assumed spread over bills | spread | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bp/yr | −4.85 bp/mo | −1.31 |
| 25 bp/yr (headline) | −3.98 bp/mo | −1.08 |
| 50 bp/yr | −3.10 bp/mo | −0.84 |
| 100 bp/yr | −1.35 bp/mo | −0.37 |

Even at a punitive 100 bp/yr financing assumption the zero fund still does not get ahead —
so the negative sign is not an artefact of being stingy with the mix's funding.

**Hedge-window sweep** (how the duration match is solved):

| window | n | L | spread | *t* | *b2* | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 126d | 214 mo | 1.419 | −0.09 bp/mo | −0.02 | +87.1 | +0.99 |
| 252d | 208 mo | 1.420 | −3.98 bp/mo | −1.08 | +110.5 | +0.84 |
| 504d | 196 mo | 1.409 | −1.18 bp/mo | −0.40 | +98.2 | +0.94 |

`L` is stable to the third decimal across lookbacks; the mean spread wobbles between −0.1
and −4.0 bp/month, which is another way of saying it is noise. `b2` stays positive and
insignificant throughout.

## Cross-check — ZROZ (PIMCO 25+ Year Zero-Coupon), 2010-12 → 2026-06, 186 months

Longer zeros still: **L = 1.549**, vol ratio 0.992. Spread **−2.06 bp/mo** (*t* = −0.46).
`b2` = **+208.7** (*t* = +1.69) on the squared net move but only **+51.7** (*t* = +0.27) on
realised variance; `a` = −11.43 bp/mo (*t* = −1.75) and −4.72 bp/mo (*t* = −0.46)
respectively. The residual duration leak is milder here (*b1* *t* = −1.40, not significant),
which is consistent with ZROZ's 25y+ mandate sitting closer to the 30-year point the hedge
is solved against. The move buckets are non-monotone (−7.3 / +3.3 / −2.3 bp/mo). Same
signs, same absence of significance on the full sample, and the two quadratic specifications
disagree by a **factor of four** — the estimate is not stable enough to bank.

**And ZROZ is where the study's only significant numbers live — for one era only.** Split at
2018 (see the census above), ZROZ 2010-2017 gives `b2` = **+403.8** (*t* = **+2.14**) on the
net move and **+618.9** (*t* = **+2.88**) on realised variance, with `a` = −17.1 / −33.2
bp/mo. That is the strongest evidence in the study, and it is also the clearest illustration
of why it is not enough: on 2018-2026 the same fund gives `b2` = **−123.5** (*t* = −1.81)
with a **positive** intercept — the convexity story running backwards — while EDV, the
headline fund, shows nothing above +1.87 in any era. An effect that appears at *t* = 2.9 in
one 84-month window of the secondary fund and inverts in the next window is a coin, not a
convexity premium. It is reported here in full rather than either buried or promoted.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports a real-tape stamp)

On a *planted* world where the long leg genuinely carries 2.5x the short leg's convexity
per unit of duration and pays 30 bp/month of carry for it, the same harness recovers
`b2` = **+260** (*t* = **+6.31**) and `a` = **−27.1 bp/mo** (*t* = **−7.41**), with a vol
ratio of 1.002 and no residual linear term. On the null — where the duration-matched mix is
convexity-matched too — `b2`'s *t* is centred at **−0.93** across 8 seeds and clears |*t*|
= 2 in **1/8**. The detector fires when there is something to find and stays quiet when
there is not, so the real-tape silence is a property of **the Treasury curve**, not of a
broken regression.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Weak.** Nearly every sign the convexity story predicts is present: across the
  full 12-cut census the quadratic coefficient is **positive in 11 of 12** fund × era ×
  specification cuts and the intercept **negative in 11 of 12**, and the fitted magnitude
  (+6.9 bp for a 25 bp month, +27.6 bp for a 50 bp month) is the right order for a
  ~7.5-year duration gap. But the headline reaches only **+0.84** (**+1.31** on realised
  variance), the bootstrap intervals straddle zero, and the raw large-move bucket is
  **negative**, not positive. Two cuts *do* clear |*t*| = 2 — ZROZ 2010-2017, at **+2.14**
  and **+2.88** — and they are reported rather than hidden; they are also one window of the
  cross-check fund fit twice, uncorrected for twelve looks, and the **adjacent era of that
  same fund flips both signs** (`b2` = −123.5, `a` = +5.09). The desk's bar is a *robust*
  |*t*| ≥ 2; this is significance that does not replicate next door, which is exactly what
  `WEAK` ("fragile to method or selection") denotes. On top of that the spread retains a
  significant **+0.72 years** of residual duration (*t* = −2.73, in both eras), so part of
  what is being measured is the 20s-30s curve rather than convexity. Directionally right,
  statistically uncertified: **Weak**, not Real. Survivorship is not an issue here (four
  named, still-listed funds and one official yield series), but **fund-selection** is: EDV
  and ZROZ are the only two US zero-coupon Treasury ETFs that survived to be testable.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to bank. The spread earns **−0.53%/yr** with a
  monthly Sharpe of **−0.21**; the fitted convexity needs a **28 bp** monthly move to repay
  its own carry cost while the median month delivers **15 bp**; the effect halves-and-halves
  again in the recent era (and turns **negative** for ZROZ there); and the number survives
  neither the change of quadratic regressor (ZROZ full sample: +209 → +52) nor the hedge
  lookback in any stable way. Costs and financing are
  immaterial — this one does not fail at the friction stage, it fails at the signal stage.
  Owning the zero-coupon fund gets you **more duration per dollar**, which is a legitimate
  reason to own it; it does not get you a convexity paycheck.
